title: Component styles come from a local CSS Module
intent: Paint follows the theme and a stylesheet reaches only what its component owns. A global stylesheet, a library's included, paints outside the palettes and reaches every element on the page, so only the bootstrap imports global ones, and only the token pipeline's three. A component may statically default-import its sibling Name.module.css, whose rules select its own classes, group them in @media, @container or @supports, set layout and typography properties and take paint only from theme tokens; framework controls keep their own focus treatment. The import opt-out covers the import's form only: a finding inside the module names its CSS line and survives a marker on the import. Global selectors, imports, cross-file composition and a stylesheet loaded through import() or import.meta.glob are refused.

runtime.rationale: A stylesheet import is a build-graph edge; the bundler compiles it into the emitted CSS, after which module authorship does not exist.

reference: A component's own layout: import styles from "./Board.module.css", one static default binding, beside the component, with className={styles.board} on a native element. Otherwise Stack, Grid and the page archetypes from @terpjs/react-core. The bootstrap imports @terpjs/contract/tokens.css, ./house-style.css and ./theme.css.
